newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends down on import deals, dollar/yen.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends down on import deals, dollar/yen.

text.p: The won ended Wednesday's trading lower against the dollar, pushed down by import settlements and the U.S. unit's strength versus the Japanese yen, traders said.
The won easily slipped below what had been seen as a strong support line of 865, and the lack of central bank intervention encouraged further dollar buying, they said.

The won closed at 868.00, against an opening of 864.80. It ranged from 864.70 to 868.80. The domestic currency closed at 864.40 on Tuesday. "The dollar demand stems from fundamental factors, such as the widening trade deficit, and won't be easily stemmed," said a local dealer.
"Dollar sentiment is very bullish. It could rise to 870 tomorrow, and if the BOK continues to take such a low profile, it could rise even further," a foreign bank dealer said.
The naming of a new finance minister in a major cabinet reshuffle had no impact on the market. "The market doesn't move on such political factors," the foreign dealer said.

Talk that off-shore funds of about $600 million would come into the market next week did not stem the dollar buying. "That amount is a drop in the bucket at this moment," the local dealer said. The won's mid-rate for Thursday was seen at 867.50, against Wednesday's 864.50.
